en.title: Trump pushes Ukraine peace plan, Europe navigates security bind
en.dek: US envoys press Russia and Ukraine on NATO rules and territorial concessions as Europe considers participation in talks
facts: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff restarted talks between Russia and Ukraine for the first time since February, when engagement halted, before meeting with Putin.
The US has asked Kyiv whether it would cede its Donbas region to Russia in exchange for NATO membership.
Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said the eastern flank of NATO must not be used as a bargaining chip, noting his country was occupied by the Soviet Union during World War II.

body: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff restarted talks between Russia and Ukraine for the first time since February, when engagement halted, before meeting with Putin. Witkoff and Kushner are expected to meet with Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on Nov 19 to discuss post-war security guarantees for Kyiv, a US official said.

The US has even asked Kyiv whether it would cede its Donbas region to Russia in exchange for membership in the NATO military alliance. The prospect of blending peace talks with security talks violates a long-held tenet for Europeans: Russia’s fighting must stop first, they say, before any discussions can be held about troop movements or NATO.

Numerous EU leaders conceded during a summit on Nov 13 that they should at least participate to keep the US happy, with some suggesting it was also time to reopen the conversation about Ukraine’s NATO membership. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys warned that the eastern flank of NATO must not be a bargaining chip, noting his country was occupied by the Soviet Union during World War II.

Russian leader Vladimir Putin is playing for time, several people said, and some argued he is waiting for European elections in 2027 that could elevate far-right figures pushing to end support for Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is encouraging Europe to come to the table, arguing there was a 'window of opportunity' to make progress in the coming months.
en.context: US envoys have recently restarted negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, pressing proposals on NATO rules and territorial concessions. European leaders are weighing participation in these talks amid concerns about security guarantees and Russia's continued military pressure.
